data_gaps.requested: A dark-matter column that visibly responds to the feedback parameters
data_gaps.why_blocked: Not a cache gap — a physics/rendering fact. The DM channel is essentially feedback-invariant on this patch: total DM mass per row = 2.792e14 / 2.807e14 / 2.794e14 Msun/h (0.5% spread) across WindE = 0.91 -> 14.37. The visible per-pixel scatter (mean |ratio-1| = 0.23 between the low and high rows) is generative stochasticity, not response. The DM column will therefore look like three near-identical images, and also closely resembles the DMO condition panel (log-log Pearson r = 0.966; the condition is the TOTAL matter column, 1.188x the DM-only mass = 1/(1-f_b)).
data_gaps.closest_alternative: Keep the DM column (the user asked for it) but make its near-invariance the POINT rather than an accident: annotate the DM header as e.g. 'DM Sigma (0.5%)' or add a one-line footer 'DM total is feedback-invariant to 0.5%; gas +20%, stars -17x across the three rows', and print the three totals in the cell's provenance print(). If a responsive matter column is wanted instead, the honest substitute is a DM/DMO-condition ratio panel or the total-matter Sigma, both computable from the same arrays.

change_spec.step: 5. Replace the two per-column norms at L449-450 with four
change_spec.detail:
cmv = plt.get_cmap("cividis").copy(); cmv.set_bad(cmv(0.0))   # zero-star pixels render as the log floor, not white
dnorm = LogNorm(vmin=np.percentile(dm3[dm3 > 0], 20), vmax=np.percentile(dm3, 99.9))
gnorm = LogNorm(vmin=np.percentile(gas3[gas3 > 0], 55), vmax=np.percentile(gas3, 99.9))   # UNCHANGED
snorm = LogNorm(vmin=np.percentile(st3[st3 > 0], 70), vmax=np.percentile(st3, 99.9))
ynorm = LogNorm(vmin=np.percentile(y3[y3 > 0], 55), vmax=np.percentile(y3, 99.9))         # UNCHANGED
Measured limits with these recipes: DM 3.276e9 -> 6.069e11 (2.27 dec), gas 1.925e9 -> 5.943e10 (1.49 dec), stars 4.068e7 -> 3.49e10 (2.93 dec), y 4.774e-9 -> 3.014e-6 (2.80 dec). RATIONALE for the two new choices: DM has ZERO empty pixels and a much larger dynamic range than gas, so the gas p55 floor would clip 55% of a perfectly well-sampled field — p20 keeps 2.27 decades with only 20% clipped. STARS are 74.6% exactly-zero (per row 0.637/0.786/0.816) and their nonzero pixels span 5.7 decades (log10 p1..p99 = 4.54..10.2), so a low floor turns the panel into uniform noise; p70 of the POOLED nonzero pixels gives 2.93 decades and leaves the surviving stellar clumps crisp. Do NOT use symlog (there are no negatives; zeros are physically 'no stars' and belong at the colormap floor), and do NOT compute the stars percentile per row — the row-to-row zero fraction IS the signal, so pooling across all three rows is mandatory (this is already the convention for gas and y).

change_spec.step: 6. Rewrite the row render loop (L451-468) for four painted columns
change_spec.detail:
COLS = [(dm3, cmv, dnorm, r"DM $\Sigma$"), (gas3, cmv, gnorm, r"gas $\Sigma$"), (st3, cmv, snorm, r"stars $\Sigma$"), (y3, plt.get_cmap("inferno"), ynorm, r"Compton $y$")]
for k, r in enumerate(RUNS3):
    axfirst = None
    for c, (arr, cm, nrm, lab) in enumerate(COLS):
        a = fig.add_subplot(gs[k, 2 + c])
        a.imshow(np.ma.masked_less_equal(arr[k], 0), origin="lower", cmap=cm, norm=nrm, rasterized=True)
        a.set_xticks([]); a.set_yticks([])
        if k == 0:
            a.text(0.5, 1.06, lab, transform=a.transAxes, ha="center", fontsize=7)
        if c == 0:
            axfirst = a
            a.text(0.04, 0.05, f"$\theta$ {ROWLB[k].replace('-', ' ')}: WindE={WE[r]:.1f}", transform=a.transAxes, fontsize=5.0, color="w", va="bottom", path_effects=[pe.withStroke(linewidth=1.2, foreground="black")])
    fig.add_artist(ConnectionPatch(xyA=(1.0, 0.5), coordsA=axc.transAxes, xyB=(0.0, 0.5), coordsB=axfirst.transAxes, arrowstyle="-|>", color="0.35", lw=0.8, shrinkA=2, shrinkB=2))
Notes: the paint arrow now terminates on the DM panel (leftmost painted column) instead of the old axg — keep one arrow per row, as now. The masked_less_equal wrapper is a no-op for DM/gas/y (no zeros) and is what makes the stars panel legal under LogNorm; it MUST be paired with cmv.set_bad or the 63-82% zero pixels render transparent (= white in the PDF). All three mass channels keep cividis (same physical quantity, M_sun/h per pixel) and y keeps inferno, matching figs 0 and 2; pe is already imported at L121.

Append the numbers that the new columns' caption depends on: print(f"halo: log10 M = {np.log10(masses[i_h]):.2f}, r200c = {r200c[i_h]:.2f} Mpc/h; runs {RUNS3} with WindEnergyIn1e51erg = " + ", ".join(f"{WE[r]:.2f}" for r in RUNS3)) ; print("patch totals [Msun/h] DM / gas / stars per row: " + " | ".join(f"{dm3[k].sum():.3e} {gas3[k].sum():.3e} {st3[k].sum():.3e}" for k in range(3))) ; print(f"mass closure (DM+gas+stars)/DMO condition = " + ", ".join(f"{(dm3[k]+gas3[k]+st3[k]).sum()/cond.sum():.4f}" for k in range(3))) ; print(f"star-occupied pixel fraction per row = " + ", ".join(f"{(st3[k]>0).mean():.3f}" for k in range(3))) ; print(f"log stretches: DM {dnorm.vmin:.3e}-{dnorm.vmax:.3e}, gas {gnorm.vmin:.3e}-{gnorm.vmax:.3e}, stars {snorm.vmin:.3e}-{snorm.vmax:.3e}, y {ynorm.vmin:.3e}-{ynorm.vmax:.3e}"). Expected output (verified): totals DM 2.792e14/2.807e14/2.794e14, gas 4.373e13/4.980e13/5.233e13, stars 7.559e12/2.215e12/4.380e11; closure 0.9966/1.0032/1.0016; star pixel fraction 0.363/0.214/0.184. Only this one figure changes; no other cell reads dm3/st3/snorm/dnorm/cmv (verified: those names appear nowhere else in the 4654-line builder).

risks: The DM column carries almost no row-to-row signal — total DM mass varies only 0.5% (2.792e14 / 2.807e14 / 2.794e14 Msun/h) across WindE 0.91 -> 14.37, and it is 96.6%-log-correlated with the DMO condition panel right next to it. A referee may read it as three redundant panels. Mitigate by stating in the caption that DM invariance is the control (gas +20%, stars -17x, DM 0.5%) rather than leaving it implicit.

LogNorm + zeros: 63.7-81.6% of the stars panel pixels are exactly 0. Without np.ma.masked_less_equal AND cmv.set_bad(cmv(0.0)), matplotlib maps them to the transparent 'bad' color, which prints as WHITE in the PDF — the high-wind row would look like a blank panel. This pairing is mandatory, not cosmetic.

The stars vmin percentile must be taken over the POOLED three-row nonzero pixels (as gas and y already are). A per-row percentile would renormalize away the very feedback signal the new column exists to show.

Panel shrinkage: adding two columns inside the fixed TWO_COL[0]=7.2 in width drops the left TNG300-Dark box from width_ratio 2.6 to 2.05 (~21% smaller). The mock render is still legible, but if the box panel is judged too small the fallback is figsize=(TWO_COL[0], 4.8) with the box spanning gs[:,0] over a taller figure, not a wider one (7.2 in is the journal column limit).

Memory: the composite npz is DEFLATE-compressed so mmap_mode='r' silently fails/raises; every key access decompresses the full 131 MB (generated_patches) or 175 MB (thermo_patches) array. Bind generated_patches[i_h] to a local ONCE per run (step 3) — repeating g['generated_patches'] three times per run would decompress ~400 MB per iteration inside a ~10 GB cgroup that also holds the 70 MB dmo_box.

Deleting the fig.text at x=1.015 changes the bbox_inches='tight' crop, so the saved PDF's aspect ratio and physical width will shift slightly. Any \includegraphics[width=...] in the LaTeX source that was tuned against the old crop should be re-checked.

The deleted right-edge text was the only in-figure pointer from fig 1 to figs 0/2. The markdown edit in step 2 keeps the '§1d (fig 2)' cross-reference in prose; make sure the paper's caption for fig 1 also still names the downstream figure, or the schematic reads as ending abruptly at the painted patches.
